questions.stem: A warehouse model maximizes profit. The run is stopped with an incumbent of 8,400 and a best bound of 8,900. A manager asks whether some plan could earn 9,000. What can you answer from these two numbers alone?

options.text: Unknown, since only a run that has finished can rule out a plan
options.says: A bound is proved during the run and holds from then on; it already rules out every plan above 8,900.

options.text: No, since the bound already rules out plans earning above 8,900
options.says: Right: the best bound covers every plan not yet ruled out, explored or not, and 9,000 is above it.

options.text: Yes, since the bound covers only the nodes explored so far
options.says: The bound is the highest LP value among the nodes still open, so it covers the unexplored plans too.

options.text: Unknown, since the optimum may sit anywhere above the incumbent
options.says: The optimum lies between the incumbent and the bound, not anywhere above the incumbent.

origin.section: A MILP Solver Keeps Two Numbers: the Best Plan Found and a Bound on Every Plan

questions.stem: A crew-cost model is minimized. Its LP relaxation is 41,200. At a stop the incumbent is 43,000 and the best bound 42,100. The run is restarted with no limit and ends OPTIMAL at 42,600. What held at the stop?

options.text: The gap was 1,800, the distance from the LP relaxation to the plan in hand
options.says: The gap is measured between the incumbent and the current best bound, 42,100, not the LP relaxation; that distance belongs to the formulation.

options.text: The gap was 900, and the plan in hand was 900 above the optimum
options.says: The gap is only an upper limit on what the incumbent leaves behind; here the optimum turned out to be 400 below it.

options.text: The gap was 500, the distance from the bound to the optimum
options.says: The optimum is unknown at the stop, so no gap can be measured to it; the gap is the bracket's width, 900.

options.text: The gap was 900, and the plan in hand was 400 above the optimum
options.says: Right: the bracket was 42,100 to 43,000, and the optimum, 42,600, turned out to be 400 below the incumbent.

origin.section: The Incumbent Rises and the Bound Falls Until They Meet

questions.stem: A minimization is stopped with an incumbent of 2,000 and a best bound of 1,600. If HiGHS and SCIP each held exactly these two numbers, which relative gaps would their logs print?

options.text: HiGHS 25% and SCIP 20%, since HiGHS divides by the bound
options.says: HiGHS divides by the incumbent: 400 / 2,000 is 20%.

options.text: Both 20%, since every solver divides by the incumbent
options.says: SCIP divides by the smaller of the two in size, here the bound: 400 / 1,600 is 25%.

options.text: HiGHS 20% and SCIP 25%, since SCIP divides by the smaller one
options.says: Right: HiGHS divides 400 by the incumbent, 2,000; SCIP divides it by the smaller number, the bound of 1,600.

options.text: Both 22.2%, since every solver divides by the average of the two
options.says: Neither solver divides by an average; HiGHS uses the incumbent and SCIP the smaller of the two.

origin.section: The Relative Gap Divides by a Number Each Solver Chooses
